anchor: No consistency, optimizer convergence, or closed-loop stability claim is made here.
annotation: The text explicitly disclaims these guarantees. The validation results must not be presented as disproving guarantees the authors did not claim. This review checks code correspondence and elementary structure; a complete proof, citation, and novelty audit remains open.

anchor: Its canonical exact encoder and decoder are $E^\star=\pi|_{\mathcal B_N^+}$ and $D^\star=\Phi_N$.
annotation: The deterministic rollout is a graph over $(x_0,\mathbf u)$. The chosen coordinate domain and smoothness hypotheses matter for formal manifold statements: an open smooth domain gives the usual graph result; closed input boxes introduce boundaries/corners, and safety-restricted sets need not be manifolds. No theorem about the supplied Part I paper is certified in this bounded review.

The runner splits whole episodes before flattening transitions and fits normalization/local regression on training data. This avoids this particular train/test transition leak. It does not establish independent coverage of closed-loop states or an effective sample size equal to the transition count; transitions within episodes are dependent.

\code{DataDrivenTransition} matches the residual standardized SiLU construction. No pendulum kinematic equation is inserted into that network. Plant-specific simulator and unit choices still enter collection/evaluation through the runner, so ``system agnostic architecture should not be expanded into ``no plant-specific harness assumptions.

anchor: The learned map is not explicitly constrained to satisfy $\widehat f_\vartheta(0,0)=0$.
annotation: The one-step normalized loss, AdamW schedule, validation checkpointing and absent equilibrium constraint match the active code. Neither free-run accuracy nor equilibrium/derivative fidelity follows from one-step loss alone. Full-budget H/E learning and uncertainty-calibration evidence remains open; oracle Gate A is not that evidence.

anchor: no additional time parameterization is learned.
annotation: Because the output copies every input and $x_0$, projection identity implies injectivity. For a smooth open-domain decoder, its Jacobian contains an identity block and has full column rank, and projection is a continuous inverse on its graph. These structural facts hold even for inaccurate learned dynamics. At $N=30$ the full chart has dimension 34; the fixed-state online search has dimension 30, as in ordinary single shooting. They do not by themselves demonstrate compression, data efficiency or novelty.

anchor: not its first input to the previously applied input.
annotation: The objective and input-rate indexing match \code{DataDrivenCEMSolver._cost}. The submitted runner specifies normalized input bounds $[-10,10]$; those were not invented by validation. All-time cart rail $\pm2.4$ m and cart recentering were reviewer-added requirements. A miss under those added requirements is a reviewer-task outcome, not a violation of an authored hard-state constraint.

anchor: Gradients are not used in this active optimizer.
annotation: Cost-only elite selection, unbiased elite standard deviation, smoothing, clipping, current-mean slot and best sampled incumbent match the active path. Three finite iterations do not certify a constrained/global optimum or successful recovery; the text correctly avoids a global-minimizer claim. The completed selected CEM diagnosis improved cost in 22/40 state/warm pairs without changing combined predicted safety (18/40). Those are selected 1.2-second oracle predictions, not a trained-H result or an attainability certificate.

anchor: This ridge regression has no intercept.
annotation: Nearest-6000 selection uses population-standardized state distance only, and the fitted linear map has no intercept, as stated. Large selected inputs, finite neighborhood size, excitation/conditioning and nonlinear regression bias still need measurement. This fitted map is not automatically the plant Jacobian at upright. The text makes no such equality claim.

Riccati $P$ is separate from the predictive terminal penalty. DARE stabilizes the fitted linear model under its usual hypotheses; it is not a nonlinear saturated/hybrid stability proof. The original oracle local gain has slow cart centering under $Q_p=.02$, but slow centering is not an authored hard recentering deadline. Selected $Q_p=2$ local-only probes do not certify the proposed hybrid entry region.

anchor: resets the stored plan to zero.
annotation: The strict switch $x^TQx<.75$, queue ordering and lack of hysteresis match the submitted wrapper. For a pure cart displacement this switch permits $|p|<\sqrt{.75/.02}\simeq6.12$ m. That explains why a reviewer rail/recentering task can disagree with the controller objective; it is not proof of an unsafe design relative to unspecified rails. No nonlinear invariant region is established.

anchor: This describes the current queue implementation exactly.
annotation: The code does retain the old plan across local intervals and always shifts by five, rather than by the actual elapsed physical samples. This is a concrete stale-warm-start concern; the specification accurately reports it. Its quantitative effect on closed-loop performance has not been isolated. OA-1 is a separate proposed oracle amendment and does not repair or change submitted H.

anchor: \code{controller_lr} is unused by the active CEM path.
annotation: The dev-profile table and its 30-step/0.6-second horizon match the submitted runner. Completed validation Gate A instead used a true-model 60-step horizon, float64 reference and 20-second development cases. The existing 29 tests and synthetic CPU/CUDA equivalence passed, conditional on the disclosed unused-CVXPY-import workaround; same-author checks do not replace independent author review.

anchor: the initial sampling box does not constrain later states.
annotation: The collection box is in the submitted runner; validation reused it for a different development stress distribution. The modulo hold rule and lack of state truncation are accurately stated. Report observed excursions, settling and tested recovery behavior as conditional diagnostics. Neither a collection box nor finitely many trajectories identifies the maximum recoverable range or the constrained viable set.

anchor: There is no online parameter adaptation.
annotation: The active path uses a transition-composed rollout and a separately data-identified switched linear law; legacy latent/autoencoder/curvature solvers are inactive. This is computationally ordinary learned-dynamics shooting in canonical coordinates. Equivalence alone does not refute geometric interpretation or establish a literature novelty verdict. External claims of superior interpretability/data efficiency should be assessed separately unless actually made in this text.

The supplied PDF transcription, original Part I hypotheses/proofs and bibliography need their own source-by-source review. No literature-backed novelty verdict or confirmed theorem/citation error is asserted here. In this bounded active-code correspondence pass, no confirmed false equation or prose/code mismatch was identified; accurate limitations and open validation needs are marked above.
